svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Four lifetimes drawn as durations: the binding, the sandbox, the call, the run
svg.desc: Four lifetimes drawn as durations on one left-to-right time axis, not as nested boxes. The topmost bar is the binding, slate because it is family code, and it spans the whole axis: one per tool, built once before any key exists, alive as long as the process, holding host configuration only and reading the scope and the thread from the host's context per call rather than storing them. Below it two teal sandbox bars with different spans overlap in time, conversation A and conversation B, each one sandbox for one key of scope, thread, agent dir and kind; they sit beside the binding rather than under it, because the nesting is real but the sandbox is not its root, and neither bar contains the binding. Inside conversation A's span three amber call bars run in sequence over the one warm sandbox, since acquire is get-or-create, and each ends in a slate tick, the finally that removes the guest path that call owns. Exactly one of the three carries a thinner, sharp-cornered run bar drawn as a process group — 0..1 per call, dispatch only — and the other two carry none, which is what the 0..1 means. Conversation B carries a single call of its own, because one binding reaches as many sandboxes as it serves conversations. Both sandbox bars outlive every call inside them and end only with the conversation, where disposal is best-effort and purge asks every registered backend, and no call bar touches either end. A caption states the relation that runs the other way: a workload shipping two tools builds two bindings against one sandbox.
